subject: BIC calculatin in Finite Mixture Model

messages.author: 5462ac1d6f0ecf93
messages.subject: BIC calculatin in Finite Mixture Model
parts:
Hi can you calculate bic as written below:

data{
   int<lower=1> K;    //number of mixture components
   int<lower=1> N;    //number of observations
   real y[N];        //observations
}
parameters{
   simplex[K] theta;
   real mu[K];
   real<lower=0> sigma[K];
}
transformed parameters {
   real ps2[K];
   real bic;
   real inclp;
  
   inclp <- 0;
   for (n in 1:N) {
      for (k in 1:K) {
         ps2[k] <- log(theta[k]) + multi_normal_log(y[n],mu[k],sigma[k]);
      }
      inclp <- inclp + log_sum_exp(ps2);
   }
   bic <- -2*inclp+K*log(N);
}
model{
   real ps[K];
   sigma ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
   mu ~ normal(0,10);
   for (n in 1:N) {
      for (k in 1:K) {
         ps[k] <- log(theta[k]) + normal_log(y[n],mu[k],sigma[k]);
      }
      increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(ps));
   }
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] BIC calculatin in Finite Mixture Model
parts:
Assuming you do optimization rather than MCMC, then almost.
BIC is based on MLE point estimates. I think you're missing
a factor of 3 because your model has (3K - 1) free parameters.

Andrew and Aki have been writing papers on better
alternatives, and have a recent paper with Jonah:

http://andrewgelman.com/2015/07/16/new-papers-on-loowaic-and-stan/

Also, if you're going to compute the log likelihood in the
transformed parameter block, you can just go ahead and use
it in the model with increment_log_prob().

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] BIC calculatin in Finite Mixture Model
parts:
Yes, you can calculate BIC with Stan if you want to.

But,

(a) you should probably use a better model-comparison
approach than BIC, and

(b) if you really must compute BIC, you need to use
Stan's optimizer, not Stan's MCMC sampling, because BIC
is based on (penalized) maximum likelihood estimates of
parameters.

You can replace the code block in the model block
with

increment_log_prob(inclp);

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] BIC calculatin in Finite Mixture Model
parts:
Instead of BIC, if you're using Matlab or R (or can get your output into R) then you can use PSIS-LOO, which you can read about at the link Bob gave. I think for Matlab the code is included in MatlabStan and for R we have a package called loo that you can install from CRAN. It also computes WAIC, although we recommend LOO.

Jonah
